newsitem.title: USA: North Sea Brent limps in late U.S. paper trading.
newsitem.headline: North Sea Brent limps in late U.S. paper trading.

text.p: The price of North Sea Brent crude oil limped in late U.S. paper trading, portending a soft reopening of London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) on Tuesday, traders said.
A full cargo of May Brent traded at $19.08 a barrel, while a series of partials changed hands at $19.00-07.
May Brent traded earlier in the day at $19.40.
The IPE settled at $19.40 on Thursday before the long Easter weekend.
The May/June spread was done at minus 11 cents over the day, and was talked in the U.S. aftermarket at minus 14-13 cents, traders said
June/July was talked late at minus five to minus three cents.
